title: Continuation policy for interrupted NDJSON streams and deterministic retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe production cases where long streamed responses containing NDJSON objects are truncated mid-object due to network glitches, proxies, or gateway timeouts. Consumers that expect a sequence of complete JSON objects (NDJSON) break on partial lines, and tool/function call handoffs can become inconsistent when a call's argument object is split. Goal: Define a deterministic continuation/resume policy for NDJSON streams that is backward-compatible with existing clients, supports deterministic retries and idempotent tool calls, and minimizes user-visible duplication or loss. Constraints: must work with streaming over HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1, not require client upgrades to parse, avoid large server-side state per request, preserve low latency for single-line responses, and integrate with existing streaming structured-output fallbacks. Proposed approach: 1) Line-level resume tokens: Append an optional resume token metadata at the end of each NDJSON line in the form: "__resume__:<hex8>" (e.g., {..json..} __resume__:a4f3c1b2). Clients can ignore this token if unknown. 2) Overlap window: On resume, server re-sends the last N characters (configurable, default 256 bytes) before the resume point; client deduplication is done by matching the resume token of the first fully received line after reconnect against tokens it already processed. 3) Partial-object marker: When truncation occurs mid-object, server emits a well-known continuation marker line: "{\"_incomplete\":true, \"resume_hint\":\"<hex8>\"}" and then closes stream. This allows clients to detect truncation without attempting to parse a corrupted JSON blob. 4) Tool-call boundaries: For tool/function calls embedded in NDJSON, the server will ensure each tool-call object includes an "idempotency_key" field when calling external tools or emitting tool-call events. On resume, the server will re-emit the full tool-call object and downstream systems must treat duplicate idempotency_key as no-op. 5) Escape handling: We will recommend a strict serialization path where any trailing resume token is separated by a space and not injected into JSON strings; server-side serializers must escape control sequences and never include the "__resume__" token inside string values. 6) Deterministic retries and fallbacks: For clients that do not implement resume semantics, server will fall back to close-on-truncation and include a final line with an explanation: "{\"_error\":\"truncated_stream\",\"recommendation\":\"retry_with_resume\"}". 7) Backpointer checksum: For high-value streams (configurable per-model/route), include a short SHA1-based checksum for a critical field (e.g., the top-level object id) inside the resume metadata to detect out-of-order or mismatched content on resume. 8) Compatibility shim: Console and SDKs will offer a compatibility parser that strips trailing resume tokens and handles overlap-window deduplication for older clients. Rollout: we will gate resume tokens behind a header (X-RI-Resume: enabled) for the first rollout phase across a subset of edge nodes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New NDJSON resume token format documented in the API spec and SDKs. 2) Server emits resume token on every complete line when X-RI-Resume is enabled. 3) When stream truncated mid-line, server emits explicit _incomplete object. 4) Resume flow: reconnect with last received token -> server replays from token with overlap window -> client deduplicates using token and receives exactly the same sequence of logical objects. 5) Tool calls contain idempotency_key and downstream treat duplicates idempotently. 6) SDK compatibility parser correctly handles overlap dedupe in integration tests. 7) No perf regression (>2% p90 latency) on short-stream workloads when resume disabled.
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer to ensure resume token never appears inside JSON strings. Integration tests: - Simulate truncated TCP connection at N different bytes to verify server emits _incomplete and resume tokens. - End-to-end: client performs resume handshake and validates deduped object sequence across reconnection. - Tool-call idempotency: simulate duplicate tool-call replays and verify downstream no-op behavior. - Backpointer checksum mismatch test to ensure server rejects resumes with inconsistent provenance. Load test: measure latency/CPU with resume enabled vs disabled across 100k short/long streams. Add fuzz tests where resume token collisions are artificially induced.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable X-RI-Resume on 5% edge nodes, SDK opt-in. Monitor error-rate, duplicate-object-rate, and client parse errors for 72h. Phase 2: enable for all edge nodes for internal clients and Quickstart SDKs; allow external customers opt-in via route config. Phase 3: default-on after 60d and deprecate old fallback messaging. Provide a migration guide and examples for popular SDKs: python, node, java.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created initial proposal after investigating several customer truncation incidents (support ticket S-17432). Attached example traces and pcap excerpts in Confluence link.

2026-03-11 - Marcelo Ruiz: Reviewed proposal. Major concerns: resume token collision probability and CDNs that strip unknown trailing tokens. Suggested adding overlap window and feature-gating via header to avoid middlebox problems.

2026-03-12 - Sofia Chen: Prototype of serializer finished (branch: feat/ndjson-resume). Verified token never appears inside strings by adding dedicated tests. Pushed initial PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimelib/pull/4182

2026-03-13 - Priya Rao: Raised an edge case where tool-call objects are streamed incrementally and downstream tool runtimes may see partial JSON — recommended ensuring idempotency_key and treating repeated tool-call ids as no-op. Added dependency on ENG-445678 (streamwise-function-boundary-repair-orchestration) for coordinated rollout.

2026-03-14 - Tomás Müller: Load test results: resume enabled shows +1.4% p50 and +2.1% p90 on long-stream workloads due to extra metadata; acceptable for canary. Noted memory tail for very large overlap windows; default 256 bytes looks safe.
